## Description

### Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 070, 071, 072.

### Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). No template names `--skip-checks`.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47).
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `--skip-checks` absent from every template and agent file; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing.

### Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` before coding; the command sequences there are the specification.
- `sc_render.render` for every template render, strict; never pipe a render into `jq`.
- Every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.

### This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, in the fixed shape above.
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

### Replay Safety
Every hook write boundary is replay-safe using the existing bead and ATM task events; no second ledger is introduced. Before each write, inspect bead metadata/events and ATM task state; if the intended same verdict/head write is already recorded, skip it, and reject a conflicting verdict or head with a typed error. A report/assignment is keyed by the role task id and verdict/head; replay may re-notify via a same-id assignment update (atm-core #1619) but may not create a second task. Injected-runner failure tests cover each boundary, including close, report, counter update, dev reopen, sanity reset/close, dev-task close and QA assignment; replay neither double-counts FAIL nor double-sends a new task, and eventually completes. The FAIL counter increments once per distinct verdict event. The close/report/assignment command ordering is explicit and any interruption resumes from recorded state. A not_reproducible fix strict-renders the report and sanity assignment using the same vars path without commit, PR number or branch.

## Acceptance criteria

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (ANC-054) `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity; the source reads only the last stack layer (or pr_target for an empty ledger) and contains no lint or test subprocess.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id.
- [ ] (ANC-057) five distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting leave `sanity_round` at 5, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the fifth, the sanity bead `in_progress` assigned to the lead, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to the lead; replaying the fifth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the second run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward`, the round's filing reviewer; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; the operational invocation scan finds no `--skip-checks` use in templates/agents; a separate help test verifies the script documents the option.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (ANC-071) `rg -n sanity_round scripts/atm-task-close.py` shows the only increment on the FAIL branch.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` does not exist and nothing references it: script and its two tests are absent; the manifest has one bj-3 owner for inventory cleanup, and composed installed-skill validation after bj-3 reports no active reference (historical changelog excluded).
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; `rg -n "atm task close .* completed" templates/dev-template.xml.j2 templates/fix-assignment.xml.j2` returns nothing.

### Validation
- `just lint` and `just test` in the atm-bd-orchestration worktree.
- `python3 -m pytest plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/tests/test_task_close.py -q`
- [ ] Injected failures and replay at every hook write boundary converge to one recorded verdict, one FAIL increment, no duplicate task creation, and eventual dev-task close/QA assignment; force both hook/dispatch assignment interleavings and verify same task id is updated/notified per atm-core #1619.

Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). No template names `--skip-checks`.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47).
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `--skip-checks` absent from every template and agent file; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing.

### Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` before coding; the command sequences there are the specification.
- `sc_render.render` for every template render, strict; never pipe a render into `jq`.
- Every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.

### This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, in the fixed shape above.
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

### Replay Safety
Every hook write boundary is replay-safe using the existing bead and ATM task events; no second ledger is introduced. Before each write, inspect bead metadata/events and ATM task state; if the intended same verdict/head write is already recorded, skip it, and reject a conflicting verdict or head with a typed error. A report/assignment is keyed by the role task id and verdict/head; replay may re-notify via a same-id assignment update (atm-core #1619) but may not create a second task. Injected-runner failure tests cover each boundary, including close, report, counter update, dev reopen, sanity reset/close, dev-task close and QA assignment; replay neither double-counts FAIL nor double-sends a new task, and eventually completes. The FAIL counter increments once per distinct verdict event. The close/report/assignment command ordering is explicit and any interruption resumes from recorded state. A not_reproducible fix strict-renders the report and sanity assignment using the same vars path without commit, PR number or branch.

## Acceptance criteria

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (ANC-054) `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity; the source reads only the last stack layer (or pr_target for an empty ledger) and contains no lint or test subprocess.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id.
- [ ] (ANC-057) five distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting leave `sanity_round` at 5, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the fifth, the sanity bead `in_progress` assigned to the lead, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to the lead; replaying the fifth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the second run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward`, the round's filing reviewer; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; the operational invocation scan finds no `--skip-checks` use in templates/agents; a separate help test verifies the script documents the option.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (ANC-071) `rg -n sanity_round scripts/atm-task-close.py` shows the only increment on the FAIL branch.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` does not exist and nothing references it: script and its two tests are absent; the manifest has one bj-3 owner for inventory cleanup, and composed installed-skill validation after bj-3 reports no active reference (historical changelog excluded).
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; `rg -n "atm task close .* completed" templates/dev-template.xml.j2 templates/fix-assignment.xml.j2` returns nothing.

### Validation
- `just lint` and `just test` in the atm-bd-orchestration worktree.
- `python3 -m pytest plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/tests/test_task_close.py -q`
- [ ] Injected failures and replay at every hook write boundary converge to one recorded verdict, one FAIL increment, no duplicate task creation, and eventual dev-task close/QA assignment; force both hook/dispatch assignment interleavings and verify same task id is updated/notified per atm-core #1619.

{"model": "jev-latest", "state": {"anchor": {"id": "ANC-022", "statement": "The atm-bd-console command must be replaced by the atm-bd console subcommand.", "scope": "edits the command name, install scripts or any caller of the console"}, "item": {"id": "item-18", "title": "", "text": "# bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds

## Description

### Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 070, 071, 072.

### Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. ## Description

### Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 070, 071, 072.

### Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). No template names `--skip-checks`.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47).
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `--skip-checks` absent from every template and agent file; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing.

### Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` before coding; the command sequences there are the specification.
- `sc_render.render` for every template render, strict; never pipe a render into `jq`.
- Every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.

### This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, in the fixed shape above.
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

### Replay Safety
Every hook write boundary is replay-safe using the existing bead and ATM task events; no second ledger is introduced. Before each write, inspect bead metadata/events and ATM task state; if the intended same verdict/head write is already recorded, skip it, and reject a conflicting verdict or head with a typed error. A report/assignment is keyed by the role task id and verdict/head; replay may re-notify via a same-id assignment update (atm-core #1619) but may not create a second task. Injected-runner failure tests cover each boundary, including close, report, counter update, dev reopen, sanity reset/close, dev-task close and QA assignment; replay neither double-counts FAIL nor double-sends a new task, and eventually completes. The FAIL counter increments once per distinct verdict event. The close/report/assignment command ordering is explicit and any interruption resumes from recorded state. A not_reproducible fix strict-renders the report and sanity assignment using the same vars path without commit, PR number or branch.

## Acceptance criteria

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (ANC-054) `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity; the source reads only the last stack layer (or pr_target for an empty ledger) and contains no lint or test subprocess.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id.
- [ ] (ANC-057) five distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting leave `sanity_round` at 5, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the fifth, the sanity bead `in_progress` assigned to the lead, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to the lead; replaying the fifth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the second run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward`, the round's filing reviewer; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; the operational invocation scan finds no `--skip-checks` use in templates/agents; a separate help test verifies the script documents the option.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (ANC-071) `rg -n sanity_round scripts/atm-task-close.py` shows the only increment on the FAIL branch.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` does not exist and nothing references it: script and its two tests are absent; the manifest has one bj-3 owner for inventory cleanup, and composed installed-skill validation after bj-3 reports no active reference (historical changelog excluded).
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; `rg -n "atm task close .* completed" templates/dev-template.xml.j2 templates/fix-assignment.xml.j2` returns nothing.

- `just lint` and `just test` in the atm-bd-orchestration worktree.
- `python3 -m pytest plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/tests/test_task_close.py -q`

The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7. Role `qa` (ANC-070, quality-mgr 20): input the verdict, the sha, the round; `bd close <qa bead>` first, then `atm task close <qa bead> completed --template qa-complete.md.j2` only if the bead close succeeded; one plain `atm send` status message to the phase lead, PASS and FAIL alike; assigns nothing.
8. `templates/task-close-vars.j2`: header-only strict template, `required_variables` per role through `defaults` and the role switch in deliverable 2; `templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2`: the sprint and checked bead ids and title, branch, PR and sha checked, round n of `max_sanity_rounds`, and one numbered line per deliverable that was NOT complete with the selected reviewer's reason verbatim, nothing else (ANC-072); `templates/rebase-required.xml.j2`: the checked bead, the branch, the recorded top it must rebase onto and the instruction to push and run the hook again (ANC-065). Example vars under `examples/task-close-vars-<role>.json`.
9. `max_sanity_rounds` in the repository configuration: `config/atm-bd-orchestration.yaml.j2` gains the key with default 5; `install.py` renders it from the consumer registry key `max_sanity_rounds` when present, else 5; `repo_config.py` exposes it (ANC-057).
10. Template close steps: `dev-template.xml.j2`, `fix-assignment.xml.j2`, `dev-sanity-template.xml.j2` and `qa-template.xml.j2` end with "run `atm-task-close.py --role <role> --vars <file>`; on `err` fix the named cause and run it again"; the dev and fix templates say the task stays open until sanity PASS, that a `task_reminder` during the wait is answered by waiting, and that a `sanity-fail` or `rebase-required` message means rebase onto the current top, push and run the hook again (dev 2, 17, 20). No template names `--skip-checks`.
11. `scripts/sanity-create-findings` deleted with `test_sanity_create_findings.py` and `test_sanity_selected.py`; `sanity-merge`, `sanity-split` and `sanity-run-history` unchanged (dev-sanity 47).
12. Tests, `scripts/tests/test_task_close.py`, with injected runners (no live bd, atm, gh or GitHub): each role's command sequence and identity per command; the vars validation failing before any git or gh call; `--skip-checks` absent from every template and agent file; `github: unavailable` fallback; the FAIL counter and the cap; the PASS refusal without a stack result; the qa role assigning nothing.

### Required Work
- Read `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` and `docs/diagrams/lifecycle.md` before coding; the command sequences there are the specification.
- `sc_render.render` for every template render, strict; never pipe a render into `jq`.
- Every subprocess is a fixed argv, never a shell string.

### This Sprint Does Not Close
- The stack bead, its pour and `validate-plan` check (bj-2); the hook only reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers`, in the fixed shape above.
- atm-bd dispatch (phase bi, unchanged): it assigns only a sanity or qa bead that `bd ready` lists with no ATM task, never a dev or fix bead (ANC-060, ANC-061).
- The link on PASS, the sanity-stack subagent and the dev-sanity prompt (bj-3); this sprint's sanity role only requires the stack result in its vars.
- The console runs tabs and the ledger producers (bj-4).

### Replay Safety
Every hook write boundary is replay-safe using the existing bead and ATM task events; no second ledger is introduced. Before each write, inspect bead metadata/events and ATM task state; if the intended same verdict/head write is already recorded, skip it, and reject a conflicting verdict or head with a typed error. A report/assignment is keyed by the role task id and verdict/head; replay may re-notify via a same-id assignment update (atm-core #1619) but may not create a second task. Injected-runner failure tests cover each boundary, including close, report, counter update, dev reopen, sanity reset/close, dev-task close and QA assignment; replay neither double-counts FAIL nor double-sends a new task, and eventually completes. The FAIL counter increments once per distinct verdict event. The close/report/assignment command ordering is explicit and any interruption resumes from recorded state. A not_reproducible fix strict-renders the report and sanity assignment using the same vars path without commit, PR number or branch.

## Acceptance criteria

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] (ANC-054) `atm-task-close.py --help` lists `--role` as mandatory with the four values; the dev-role check list is exactly: open PR exists, pushed head equals clean HEAD and PR head, and HEAD descends from the current top (`layers[-1]`, falling back to `pr_target` for empty layers); a nonempty-stack fixture with a mismatched lower layer and current top ancestor passes; an unlinked PR passes pre-link frozen/commit gates and is linked after sanity; the source reads only the last stack layer (or pr_target for an empty ledger) and contains no lint or test subprocess.
- [ ] (ANC-058) a vars file missing a role-required field fails with `VARS.MISSING` before any git or gh call; strict render fixtures cover every role/template using one identical vars path; rendered dev, sanity and QA body task ids equal their command `--task-id` values; a not_reproducible fix with no commit/pr_number/branch renders its report and sanity assignment end to end.
- [ ] (ANC-051) in the test's recorded calls, every `atm task assign` and the close of the checked bead's task carry `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead from .atm-bd/phase-x.toml>`; every `bd` write carries `--actor <caller>`.
- [ ] (ANC-052, ANC-055) a dev-role run in a scratch repository with fixture bd and atm: the bead is closed, the sanity task is assigned in the same hook invocation immediately after the bead close using the same vars file, the completion report follows the pair, and no `atm task close <dev task> completed` was issued.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a sanity-role PASS run assigns the qa bead to the qa member as the lead and closes the checked bead's task as the lead.
- [ ] (ANC-056, ANC-072) a sanity-role FAIL run issues exactly one `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2`, reopens the checked bead to its assignee and resets the sanity bead to open/unassigned, creates no bead, and the rendered message lists exactly the undone deliverables with their reasons and the sprint id.
- [ ] (ANC-057) five distinct FAIL verdicts with no `max_sanity_rounds` setting leave `sanity_round` at 5, the checked bead closed and not reopened on the fifth, the sanity bead `in_progress` assigned to the lead, and exactly one `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` send to the lead; replaying the fifth FAIL sends no second notice; with `max_sanity_rounds: 2` the second run does the same.
- [ ] (ANC-053) a controlled `not_reproducible` fix: the hook assigns sanity with the stack top's branch and head; a sanity PASS with `outcome: not_reproducible` and no stack result closes the sanity bead and the fix's task and assigns QA with `carry_forward`, the round's filing reviewer; no `SANITY.NOT_STACKED`, no layer.
- [ ] (ANC-059) with the GitHub runner raising, a dev-role run exits ok with `"github": "unavailable"` after three attempts; the operational invocation scan finds no `--skip-checks` use in templates/agents; a separate help test verifies the script documents the option.
- [ ] (ANC-070) a qa-role run with verdict FAIL closes the qa bead then the task, sends the lead one status message and issues no `atm task assign`.
- [ ] (ANC-071) `rg -n sanity_round scripts/atm-task-close.py` shows the only increment on the FAIL branch.
- [ ] (dev-sanity 47) `scripts/sanity-create-findings` does not exist and nothing references it: script and its two tests are absent; the manifest has one bj-3 owner for inventory cleanup, and composed installed-skill validation after bj-3 reports no active reference (historical changelog excluded).
- [ ] the four assignment templates render strictly with their example vars and name the hook as the close step; `rg -n "atm task close .* completed" templates/dev-template.xml.j2 templates/fix-assignment.xml.j2` returns nothing.

### Validation
- `just lint` and `just test` in the atm-bd-orchestration worktree.
- `python3 -m pytest plugins/atm-bd-orchestration/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/tests/test_task_close.py -q`
- [ ] Injected failures and replay at every hook write boundary converge to one recorded verdict, one FAIL increment, no duplicate task creation, and eventual dev-task close/QA assignment; force both hook/dispatch assignment interleavings and verify same task id is updated/notified per atm-core #1619.

{"model": "jev-latest", "state": {"anchor": {"id": "ANC-022", "statement": "The atm-bd-console command must be replaced by the atm-bd console subcommand.", "scope": "edits the command name, install scripts or any caller of the console"}, "item": {"id": "item-18", "title": "", "text": "# bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds

## Description

### Goal
One script, `atm-task-close.py --role <dev|fix|sanity|qa> --vars <file>`, is the only way a dev, fix, sanity or qa task completes (task-close-hook.md 1). The agent never runs `bd close` or `atm task close ... completed` by hand for those roles. The script checks the minimum, closes the bead, reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead. Governing text: `docs/requirements/task-close-hook.md` items 1 to 19, `dev.md` 2, 4, 15, 17, 20, 24, `dev-sanity.md` 11, 13, 28, 29, 32, 47, `quality-mgr.md` 20, `team-lead.md` 14, 15, 21, 23, 24, 28. Anchors: ANC-051, 052, 053, 054, 055, 056, 057, 058, 059, 060, 070, 071, 072.

### Deliverables
1. `scripts/atm-task-close.py`: one `--role` argument, mandatory, one of `dev`, `fix`, `sanity`, `qa`; `--vars <file>`; `--skip-checks` described only in `--help` as "skips the PR and stack checks. Do NOT use without permission from the phase lead." and named in no template or prompt (ANC-059). Result is JSON on stdout, `{"ok": {...}}` or `{"err": {"code", "message", "fix"}}`, exit code mirroring it; every `err` names the exact fix (task-close-hook.md 3). No ledger of its own.
2. Input validation (ANC-058): the vars file is the sc-compose `--vars` payload the role's templates already take; the script validates the unchanged shared vars file with a strict render before any check. The single contract defines distinct `dev_task_id`, `sanity_task_id`, `qa_task_id`, `checked_bead`, `sanity_bead`, and `qa_bead`; `task_id` always means the bead whose ATM task is being closed by the current role template, and assignment templates render their explicit destination id. The role/template matrix lists every required field and nonempty rule: dev completion requires phase, sprint, dev task/bead id, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, base, lint_command, primary_checkout, report inventory, commit, pr_number, pr_url; fix completion has the same fields when fixed, while `outcome=not_reproducible` requires phase, sprint, fix task/bead id, outcome, evidence file:line, and report inventory, and forbids requiring commit/pr_number/branch; sanity assignment requires sanity_task_id, checked_bead, branch, worktree_path, pr_target, verdict inputs and round; QA assignment requires qa_task_id, qa_bead, base, commit, round, reviewer and policy fields, with carry_forward only for fixes; completion reports require their role-specific task id, verdict/outcome, report inventory and status fields. Optional fields are omitted by role/outcome, not supplied as empty defaults. The identical vars path is strict-rendered through the dev->sanity->QA sequence and every rendered body id is asserted equal to the matching command `--task-id` value.
3. Identity (ANC-051): `atm task assign` and the close of the dev's task run with `ATM_IDENTITY=<lead>` and `ATM_TEAM=<team>` set on that one subprocess only, `lead` read from `.atm-bd/phase-<x>.toml` and the team from `.atm.toml`; every other `bd` and `atm` write runs as the caller with `--actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`. The script never changes its own environment.
4. Role `dev` and `fix` (ANC-054, task-close-hook.md 7 to 12): after the vars, checks exactly three things: an open PR exists for `branch`; pushed `origin/<branch>` equals clean HEAD and is the PR head; and HEAD descends from the current stack top, defined as the last `metadata.layers` entry, or `pr_target` when the ledger has no layers. bj-1 reads the stack bead's `metadata.layers` with `bd show <stack bead> --json`, an array of `{branch, pr, head, base, linked}` (the shape bj-2 deliverable 2 defines); its tests inject a stack-bead JSON of that shape and import nothing from bj-2, so the two sprints stay parallel. The PR base is not a fourth check, and with a nonempty ledger the check never uses a static branch. `assignment-gates.py` retains only frozen/commit checks that can run before linking; it does not require an already linked PR. No lower layer is checked, and the hook runs no lint or tests (ANC-054). On pass: `bd update <bead> --set-metadata commit=<sha> pr_number=<n> pr_url=<url>`; `bd close <bead> --reason "dev complete at <sha>"` (`fixed at <sha>` for a fix); in the same hook invocation, `bd close <dev bead>` is immediately followed by `atm task assign <dev-sanity member> --task-id <sanity bead> --template dev-sanity-template.xml.j2 --vars <same file>` as the lead, with no command, report, or lead action between those two writes (ANC-052); the dev-complete/fix-complete report is sent after the pair. The dev's ATM task stays open (ANC-055). The sanity bead is `metadata.sanity_bead` of the checked bead when present, else the open `stage:dev-sanity` bead whose `metadata.dev_bead` is the checked bead; none: `err` naming the lead. Fix outcome `not_reproducible`: the PR and head checks are skipped, `bd close --reason "not reproducible: <file:line>"`, the same report and the same sanity assignment, whose `branch` and `commit` are the current stack top (the last `metadata.layers` entry's branch and head, or `pr_target` and its head when the ledger is empty), so `sanity-split` runs unchanged.
5. GitHub unreachable or rate limited (ANC-059): not a failure; the PR check falls back to the local checks of deliverable 4, the result records `github: unavailable`, and sanity is assigned. Retry a failed GitHub call three times before falling back.
6. Role `sanity` (task-close-hook.md 13 to 17): input the verdict (`PASS`, `FAIL`, `CANNOT_RUN`), the sha, the selected undone deliverables with their reasons, the checked bead and its assignee, the group's QA bead, and for PASS the stack result from the link (`stacked`, new top, nullable `stack_number` for a singleton stack). A PASS close without a stack result is refused with `err` code `SANITY.NOT_STACKED` naming the link as the fix (sanity-stack.md 13), except a PASS on a `not_reproducible` fix, which has no layer and is accepted without one. PASS: `bd close <sanity bead> --reason "PASS at <sha>"`; `atm task close <checked bead> completed` as the lead; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2`; `atm task assign <qa member> --task-id <qa bead> --template qa-template.xml.j2 --vars <file>` as the lead, with `base` the PR base, `commit`, `round`, `reviewer` and `policy`, and for a fix bead `carry_forward` (ANC-053). FAIL: `bd update <sanity bead> --set-metadata sanity_round=<n+1>` first. While the new count is below `max_sanity_rounds` (repository configuration, default 5 when unset): reopen the checked dev/fix bead to its assignee and reset the claimed sanity bead to `--status open --assignee ""` before finishing the sanity task; `atm send <assignee> --template sanity-fail.xml.j2 --vars <file>` on the dev's open task; `atm task close <sanity bead> completed --template dev-sanity-complete.md.j2` with verdict FAIL; no finding bead, no child bead, no new task, no new layer (ANC-056, ANC-072). When the count reaches `max_sanity_rounds`: the checked bead stays closed, the sanity bead stays `in_progress` and is assigned to the phase lead (`bd update <sanity bead> --assignee <lead>`), so neither `bd ready` nor atm-bd assigns it again, nothing is reopened, the script sends the lead `SANITY.ROUND_CAP` with the undone deliverable numbers and closes the sanity task with verdict FAIL; the dev's task stays open (ANC-057). The lead resumes by reopening the checked bead to its dev and resetting the sanity bead to open and unassigned. CANNOT_RUN: sanity bead open and unassigned, task `refused` (dev-sanity 31). A `rebase-required` outcome is not a close: the script exposes no path for it that touches `sanity_round` (ANC-071).
7.
